The study aimed to compare the effects of Mindfulness-based Stress Reduction (MBSR) and Internet-delivered Mindfulness-based Stress Reduction (iMBSR) on burden of psychosomatic symptoms of nurses working at Al-Alhamzeh general hospital, Aldiwaniyeh, Iraq.

title: Impact of Age at Surgery on Perioperative Outcomes After Posterior Spinal Fusion for Neuromuscular Scoliosis
creator: Vivien Chan, Prudhvi Kodali, Sophie Nuytten, Justin L Reyes, Mehdi Elfilali, Michael G Vitale, Zeeshan M Sardar, David L Skaggs
description: BackgroundWhile surgical outcomes for posterior spinal fusion (PSF) for pediatric patients with neuromuscular scoliosis (NMS) have been well described, less is known about how perioperative outcomes differ when surgery is performed later, during young adulthood. The purpose of this study was to compare perioperative outcomes between adolescents and young adults undergoing PSF for NMS using a large, multi-institutional clinical registry.

title: Effect of animation-based edutainment compared with pamphlet-based education on hand hygiene and HAI prevention among surgical patients: a quasi-experimental study
creator: Raziyeh Ghafouri, Zahra Azizi, Zeinab Asghari
description: SummaryBackgroundHealthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are among the most common and serious complications in healthcare settings. Engaging patients in infection prevention through effective educational interventions is a key strategy for reducing the risk of HAIs. This study aimed to compare the effects of animation-based edutainment and pamphlet-based education on hand hygiene practices and HAI prevention among surgical patients.

title: Ablation of CDK6 and STAT5B rewires T cell developmental dynamics and prevents ALK+ lymphoma formation
creator: Jonatan Kendler, Maximilian Sexl, Alessia Schirripa, Elisabeth Gamper, Hager El Kersh, Barbara Maurer, Reinhard Grausenburger, Klavdija Krause, Dua Shahid, Alexander Pichler, Giorgia Damonte, Tania Brandstoetter, Michaela Prchal-Murphy, Stefania Massari, Sabine Lagger, Lukas Kenner, Richard Moriggl,
description: CDK6 and STAT5B are well-established oncogenic drivers, but their interplay during transformation remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that simultaneous genetic deletion of Cdk6 and Stat5b in an NPM-ALKTg/+ mouse model completely prevents tumor formation. Immature DN2/3 thymocytes are identified as the cellular origin of ALK-driven malignancy.

title: Prediction of HIF-1α expression in endometrial carcinoma by enhanced T2 ∗ weighted angiography and dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging
creator: Zongyuan Xie, Liangjie Lin, Changjun Ma, Ailian Liu
description: PurposeTo explore the value of quantitative imaging parameters by enhanced T2 * weighted angiography (ESWAN) and dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) for evaluating the expression of Hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) in endometrial carcinoma (EC).MethodsData from 122 patients with EC confirmed by clinical pathology were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study
creator: Jean-Sébastien Hulot, Pierre-Yves Hervé, Nicolas Girerd, Frédérique Chézalviel-Guilbert, Philip Janiak, Pierre Boutouyrie, Jean-Joseph Christophe, Ariel Cohen, Thibaud Damy, Liliane Berkani, Kevin Duarte, Caroline Fraslon, Hüseyin Firat, Olivier Hanon, Richard Isnard, Guillaume Jondeau, Elie Moussea
description: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for over half of heart failure cases but remains poorly defined due to its clinical heterogeneity. In the prospective PACIFIC-Preserved cohort (NCT04189029, n = 155), we applied multimodal deep phenotyping, including high-throughput proteomics, and unsupervised machine learning to identify biologically distinct HFpEF subgroups.

title: Sero-catalytic and spatial modeling of dengue virus force of infection in Timor-Leste
creator: Paul Arkell, Filipe de Neri Machado, Anna Vicco, Victoria M. Cox, Maria Y. Tanesi, Deolindo Ximenes, Wes Hinsley, Frederico Bosco, Nelia Gomes, Tessa Oakley, Vanessa Solano, Sarah L. Sheridan, Michael David, Salvador Amaral, Luzia Freitas, Anthony DK Draper, Nevio Sarmento, Endang Soares da Silva, L
description: Dengue virus (DENV) infection causes significant morbidity and mortality across tropical and sub-tropical regions, including in Timor-Leste. In this study we present the results of a national, population-representative serological survey, used to determine the drivers of observed variations in DENV force-of-infection (FOI, i.e. the average annual per-capita risk of infection for a susceptible person) at high spatial resolution.

title: On-demand design of controlled-release systems using an expert-mimic AI framework
creator: Ying Qin, Rushuang Zhou, Yali Ming, Bohao Li, Yuning Hu, Donglin Sui, Jingxuan Liu, Hang Wang, Guanghui Ma, Yuedong Yang, Yining Dong, Yufei Xia
description: Navigating a vast formulation-preparation design space that is highly sensitive to perturbations makes trial-and-error approaches inefficient and costly for diverse clinical needs. Here, we introduce an expert-mimic AI framework called E-MAF that integrates a process-aware surrogate with an optimized genetic algorithm to emulate coarse-to-fine reasoning, autonomously generating lab-ready designs tailored to desired release profiles.

title: Centralised management of Barrett’s oesophagus surveillance: assessing progression risk and management
creator: Nicola B Raftery, Cian Muldoon, Ciara Ryan, Jacintha O’Sullivan, Dermot O’Toole, John V Reynolds, Jessie A Elliott, the National Barrett’s Oesophagus Registry and Scientific Network
description: ssion risk within Ireland’s National Barrett’s Esophagus Registry and Bioresource surveillance network (2). We appreciate their positive comments on the novelty of this study, and the potential value of such a centralised quality-assured programme with high data capture, and specialist endoscopy and pathology.

title: Association between coffee consumption and risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism – Results from the Trøndelag Health Study and Tromsø Study
creator: Melliane M. Olsen, Sigrid K. Brækkan, Kristian Hveem, Kjersti Grønning, John-Bjarne Hansen
description: BackgroundEpidemiological studies have shown that coffee consumption is associated with a lowered risk of incident venous thromboembolism (VTE). No previous study has explored whether coffee consumption influences the risk of VTE recurrence.ObjectivesThis study aimed to investigate whether the amount of coffee consumption (cups/d) is associated with the risk of VTE recurrence in a population-based cohort of incident VTEs.

title: Editorial for the Special Issue on Cholesterol Crystal Embolization☆
creator: George S Abela
description: d others have even referred to them as a postmortem artifact. However, more recent studies have elucidated a more active role of CCs. In fact, the articles presented in this Special Issue on Cholesterol Crystal Emboli tell a different story.

title: A triple protein-based ELISA for differential detection of ASFV antibodies
creator: Shuai Zhang, Yuzhu Zuo, Wenyuan Gu, Yunhuan Zhao, Ying Liu, Jinghui Fan
description: African swine fever (ASF) caused by the ASF virus (ASFV) is a severe and highly contagious viral disease that poses a significant threat to the global pig industry. As no vaccines or effective drugs are available to aid prevention and control, early detection is crucial.

title: Polytetrafluoroethylene utensils as a source of micro- and nanoplastics: Insights from a Drosophila model
creator: Mohamed Alaraby, Doaa Abass, Elham Farghal Elkady, Raquel Egea, Antonia Velázquez, Alba Hernández, Ricard Marcos
description: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), widely used in household products and cookware, can release particles into food, posing potential health risks. The biological interactions of the resulting micro- and nanoplastics (MNPLs) remain poorly understood but can be clarified by linking structural and physiological effects with transcriptomic changes.

title: Yogurt consumption and risk of accelerated aging: A population-based study from the NHANES 2003–2006
creator: Xinghai Yue, Hongfei Liu, Wenzhao Guo, Yuhang Gao, Shaoshun Shi
description: IntroductionYogurt consumption is beneficial to health, but its association with aging remains unclear. This study aims to explore the relationship between yogurt consumption and aging using data from the 2003–2006 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES).MethodsWe used data from 4,056 participants to examine the relationship between yogurt consumption and aging.

title: Effects of dietary Zanthoxylum bungeanum seed powder on growth performance, immune function, and cecal microbiota in broilers
creator: Zhijin Hu, Huatao Liu, Yuxi Shen, Fu Feng, Zhihong Sun, Weizhong Sun, Yetong Xu, Jiaman Pang, Zhiru Tang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study was conducted to evaluate the effects of Zanthoxylum bungeanum seed powder (ZBS) on growth performance, immune function, and cecal microbiota in 817 broilers. A total of 260 one-day-old 817 broilers were randomly assigned to 4 treatment groups (CON, ZBS1, ZBS2, and ZBS3) with 5 replicates per treatment and were fed diets containing 0, 1%, 2%, or 3% ZBS, respectively, for 63 d.

title: Contribution of social activity participation to the relationship between sensory impairment, physical performance and cognitive decline: a longitudinal study in China
creator: Lei Lei, Yinuo Zhou, Lizhen Ye, Yanfang Yang
description: ObjectivesThis study examined the impact of sensory impairment (hearing and/or vision) combined with poor physical performance on cognitive decline and assessed whether social activity participation mediated this relationship.MethodsMultilevel models were used to explore the relationships between sensory impairment, physical performance, their combination, and cognitive decline. A multilevel mediation model analyzed the mediating effect of social activity participation.

title: Dogmas in Obstetrics: Evidence-Based Standards, Clinical Judgement and Patient-Centred Care
creator: Holger Maul, Werner Rath
description: Obstetrics requires standards, guidelines and established pathways to support physiological birth and to manage rare emergencies reliably. Standards become problematic, however, when they are detached from their evidentiary basis, original indication or individual clinical context and are applied as dogmas.

title: High-speed electric-scooter crash causing a tibial spine fracture with physeal extension in an adolescent: a case report
creator: Abir Manni, Yacine Zouirech, Mounir Kisra
description: Tibial spine fractures are pediatric anterior cruciate ligament–equivalent avulsion injuries that can be radiographically subtle, leading to delayed or missed diagnosis. We report the case of a healthy 14-year-old girl who sustained a high-speed electric-scooter crash, landing on both knees in flexion.

title: Preoperative MRI-derived fat fraction is linked to survival after liver transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Jialin Gao, Donghua Zhang, Tao Jiang, Decai Yu
description: Background and aimsLiver transplantation (LT) is a curative option for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, HCC recurrence and the limited accuracy of current morphological criteria remain unresolved issues. This study investigated the association between preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–derived fat fraction (FF) and survival in patients with HCC undergoing LT.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 42 patients with HCC who underwent orthotopic LT.

title: Isolation and characterization of a Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus from fish pond water
creator: Qian-Ming Hong, Kai Yuan, Meng-En Zhang, Xin-Rui Yang, Qi Chen, Shi-Wei Xu, Wan-Yi Chen, Shi-Xin Qian, Yu-Tao Miao, Zhi-Ming Zhu, Yi-Hong Chen
description: IntroductionThe intricate habitats of aquatic organisms, coupled with the prevalence of pathogens, contribute to a high incidence of various diseases, particularly bacterial infections. Consequently, the formulation of sustainable and effective disease management strategies is crucial for the thriving aquaculture sector.Methods and resultsIn this investigation, a strain of Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus, designated B. bacteriovorus FWA, was isolated from a freshwater fish pond.

title: Precision chest sculpting: 3D-customized silicone implants and computer-aided design assisted reconstruction for pectus excavatum - a single center experience
creator: Daniela Geisler, Christoph Müller, Jose R. Matilla, Clemens Aigner, Christine Radtke
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryPectus excavatum correction in adults is often pursued for functional and aesthetic reasons, yet modified Nuss and Ravitch procedures may be invasive and can leave residual anterior chest wall contour deformities. We report a single-center retrospective consecutive case series of aesthetic chest wall correction using patient-specific silicone implants designed with computed tomography (CT)-based three-dimensional (3D) computer-aided design (CAD), with descriptive assessment of postoperative patient-reported and morphological outcomes.

title: Weizmannia coagulans BC99 alleviates hyperuricemia and oxidative stress via DAF-16/SKN-1 activation in Caenorhabditis elegan
creator: Yinyin Gao, Cheng Li, Junfei Li, Mengyao Duan, Xuan Li, Lina Zhao, Ying Wu, Shaobin Gu
description: IntroductionHyperuricemia (HUA) refers to the presence of excess uric acid (UA) in the blood, which increases the risk of chronic kidney disease and gout. Probiotics have the potential to alleviate HUA.MethodsThis study established a hyperuricemia model using Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans), and studied the anti-hyperuricemia activity and potential mechanisms of Weizmannella coagulans BC99 (W.

title: Empowering youth and ensuring health: utilization of youth friendly service among preparatory school students in Gambella, Southwest Ethiopia
creator: Nardos Hailu, Benti Negero, Keno Melkamu, Yawkal Tsega
description: BackgroundYouth is a period with exposure to high risk of reproductive health (RH) problems. Despite, several strategies designed to solve these problems, youths are experiencing unsafe abortion, unintended pregnancy, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) so far. The utilization of Youth Friendly Services (YFS) and its determinants has not been well studied in Gambella so far.

title: Older adults in more disadvantaged neighborhoods exhibit brain vascular dysfunction
creator: Kevin W Law, Allison C Engstrom, Trevor Lohman, Melanie Quiring, Arunima Kapoor, John Paul M Alitin, Danny JJ Wang, Aimée Gaubert, Kathleen Rodgers, Elizabeth Head, Celina I Valencia, Jillian L Joyce, Farrah Ferrer, Daniel A Nation
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights•This study examines brain microvascular differences in older adults at rest.•Neighborhood deprivation is associated with reduced cerebrovascular reactivity.•Findings are independent of Alzheimer’s disease-related pathology.Keywords: Neighborhood disadvantage, Cerebrovascular reactivity, Brain health, Vascular dementia, Health disparities

Introduction

While neighborhood disadvantage, a social determinant of health, is implicated as an environmental risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia [1,2], little is known about the biological mechanisms involved. Meanwhile, dementia incidence is increasing, with annual new cases in the U.S. expected to double by 2060 [3].

title: Understanding the defense mechanism of Allium plants through the onion isoallicin-omics study
creator: Heejung Cho, Ji Yeon Park, Duck Hyun Kim, JiWon Han, Karthi Natesan, Min-Seon Choi, Seon-Kyeong Lee, Jiseon Kim, Kun Cho, Byoung Ohg Ahn
description: Onion (Allium cepa L.) is an important seasoning vegetable worldwide. It belongs to the Allium genus, which produces distinctive flavor compounds, allicin/isoallicin. It has been known that allicin/isoallicin is produced upon cell damage by vacuole-localized alliinase releasing. Pungent isoallicin and lachrymaroty factor (LF) are unique features of onions.

title: Acupoint catgut embedding exerts node-dependent effects on leptin resistance–related signaling and the ghrelin–GOAT pathway in obese mice
creator: Qiwang Yang, Han Yang, Jinjiao Zhang, Nenggui Xu, Chuanwu Zhu, Wei Yi, Hanqing Huang
description: BackgroundObesity is a major metabolic health problem with limited effective treatments. Acupoint catgut embedding (ACE) has shown therapeutic potential; however, its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ACE on leptin resistance and the Ghrelin-GOAT pathway in obese mice.MethodsDiet-induced obesity was established in C57BL/6 J mice.

title: Simulating water and salt changes in the root zone of salt–alkali fragrant pear and the selection of the optimal surface drip irrigation mode
creator: Yanjie Li, Ping Gong, Xinlin He, Hongguang Liu, Zhijie Li, Ling Li, Chunxia Wang, Qiang Xu, Quan Chen, Jie Wei, Ping Lin, Xuyong Yu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Faced with the increasingly serious problem of water scarcity, developing precise irrigation strategies for crops in saline alkali land can effectively reduce the negative effects of low water resource utilization. Using a model to simulate the dynamic changes in soil water and salt environment in the root zone of fragrant pear trees in saline alkali land, and verifying them from a production practice perspective with comprehensive benefits as the goal, can optimize the irrigation amount and irrigation technology elements of saline alkali

title: Capturing affective states in everyday life - Comparing psychometric properties of two affect measures
creator: Matthias F Limberger, Lisa M Störkel, Johanna Hepp, Inga Niedtfeld, Markus Reichert, Philip S Santangelo, Lisa-Marie Hartnagel, Oksana Berhe, Andreas Meyer-Lindenberg, Heike Tost, Ulrich W Ebner-Priemer
description: E-diary items and scales face three contradicting challenges, originating from their repeated assessment: To achieve high compliance and to limit participant's burden a minimal number of items is aspired, to achieve reliability on a momentary level more items per scale are advantageous.

title: Reactive Oxygen Species Formation in Paddy Soils under Alternating Redox Conditions: An Iron-Microbe Synergy Driving Mechanism and Environmental Impacts
creator: Zhiwei Sun, Xinxin Wang, Xinyue Wu, Xinran Zhang, Xinya Li, Ru Wang, Xiaomeng Wang, Guanyu Zheng
description: Alternating wetting and drying cycles in paddy soils drive active biogeochemical processes and profoundly influence pollutant migration and transformation. This study systematically investigates the formation and mechanisms of reactive oxygen species (ROS) under anaerobic–aerobic alternation in five typical paddy soils, as well as their implications for the attenuation of tetracycline (TC) and associated antibiotic resistance genes.

title: Red cell distribution width to albumin ratio is associated with asthma risk: a population-based study
creator: Jinzhen Ding, Yixiang Zhang, Xiaoyang Chen
description: BackgroundThe red cell distribution width to albumin ratio (RAR), a newly identified biomarker of inflammation, has been linked to a variety of inflammatory diseases. Asthma, a major burden on global health, is an inflammatory airway disease that is profoundly affected by inflammation. This study primarily sought to examine the influence of RAR on the risk of developing asthma.

title: Unveiling the Catalytic Pyrolysis Behavior and Kinetics of Epoxy Resin over Niobium Oxide-Tailored ZSM‑5 Zeolites
creator: Shangpeng Pan, Hengbin Zhang, Rui Shan, Xinyue Liang, Jun Zhang, Chengyu Li, Taoli Huhe, Xiang Ling, Yong Chen
description: The sustainable recycling of thermosetting epoxy resin (ER) waste remains a critical environmental challenge. While fast pyrolysis offers a viable upcycling route, the direct thermal degradation of ER predominantly yields low-value, oxygen-rich phenolic compounds. In this study, a series of hierarchical niobium oxide-tailored ZSM-5 zeolites (xNb-ZSM) were synthesized to promote the selective catalytic pyrolysis of ER into high-value aromatic hydrocarbons.

title: Potential candidates from a functional food Zanthoxyli Pericarpium (Sichuan pepper) for the management of hyperuricemia: high-through virtual screening, network pharmacology and dynamics simulations
creator: Meilin Chen, Xiaomei Chen, Qinghong Chen, Chenyang Chu, Shuxuan Yang, Chuanghai Wu, Yanting You, Andrew Hung, Angela Wei Hong Yang, Xiaomin Sun, Lin Zhou, Xiaoshan Zhao, Hong Li, Yanyan Liu
description: IntroductionHyperuricemia (HUA) is a metabolic syndrome caused by purine metabolism disorders. Zanthoxyli Pericarpium (ZP) is a medicinal and food homologous plant, and its ripe peel is used to treat diseases and as a spice for cooking. Some studies have shown that ZP can inhibit the formation of xanthine oxidase and reduce the production of uric acid.

title: Extrapolation steps in quantitative in vitro to in vivo extrapolation to advance in vitro-based chemical risk assessment for human health
creator: M.J.M. Benschop, J. Minnema, E.E.J. Kasteel, A.S. Kienhuis, A.G. Oomen, J. Vriend, R.H.S. Westerink, A. Zwartsen, B.G.H. Bokkers
description: The transition towards Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) aims at increasing human relevance and efficiency of chemical risk assessment, by using human-based in vitro and in silico methods. Quantitative in vitro to in vivo Extrapolation (QIVIVE) is central to this approach and enables the derivation of health-based guidance values (HBGV) from in vitro data.

title: HOMA-beta independently predicts survival in patients with advanced cancer on treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors
creator: Mayu Watanabe, Jun Eguchi, Atsushi Takamoto, Hiromitsu Kanzaki, Yohei Noda, Syunsuke Kagawa, Jun Wada
description: BackgroundAlthough immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are effective cancer drugs, ICI-induced diabetes is a rare but a life-threatening adverse event for patients. The deleterious action of ICI on pancreatic beta-cell function is a concern. However, the influence of ICI on insulin synthesis and secretion in patients with cancer without diabetes remains unknown.MethodsThis study included 87 patients diagnosed with advanced cancer.

title: Kinetic Control of Rare Earth Element Separation via Interfacial Solvent Extraction and Low-Gradient Magnetic Fields
creator: Bailey Lake, Theo Siegrist, Hadi Mohammadigoushki, Munir Humayun, Jamel Ali
description: The production of energy-efficient technologies and advanced electronics requires high-purity critical minerals, such as individually separated rare earth elements (REEs). Chemical REE separation processes rely on small differences in physicochemical properties (i.e., ionic charge and radii) to transport selective metal ions across liquid–liquid interfaces, making selective separation time-consuming and expensive.

title: Reference ranges for complete blood count in children and adolescents with Down syndrome
creator: Martina Lattuada, Giulia Capitoli, Marco Casati, Alessandra Lazzerotti, Oscar Maglia, Giulia Maria Ferrari, Chiara Fossati, Andrea Biondi, Alessandro Cattoni, Paola Corti
description: IntroductionDown syndrome (DS) is linked to unique hematopoietic characteristics that affect complete blood count (CBC) parameters. Accurate reference ranges are essential for proper CBC interpretation in this population.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed 2,627 CBCs from 481 DS patients, aged 31 days to 18 years, at a tertiary care center in Italy.

title: Wide-Angle Stable Transmissive Focusing Metasurfaces for OAM Vortex Waves in Wireless Communications
creator: Yi Zhong, Luyao Wang, Yifei Wang, Jiayun Yu, Xiaojun Huang
description: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) vortex waves have become a promising technology for future 6G high-capacity wireless communications. However, the inherent propagation divergence and performance degradation under angular deviation severely restrict their practical applications. This paper proposes a transmissive focusing metasurface that maintains stable OAM vortex wave generation under angular deviation.

title: Disrupting shadow in the prothoracic gland induced larval development arrest in the fall armyworm Spodoptera frugiperda
creator: Mian-Zhi Wu, Shu-Ting Fan, Yuan-Chen Zhang, Jin-Fang Tan, Guan-Heng Zhu
description: IntroductionThe juvenile hormone (JH) and 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) are the central regulating hormones of insect development. The timing of their secretion usually leads to developmental transitions.MethodsThe developmental transitions were evaluated via the starvation treatment and the expressions of two key metamorphosis inducing factor in Spodoptera frugiperda.

title: Rift Valley Fever outbreaks in the East African Community: insights from ProMed data (2010–2024)
creator: Pacifique Ndishimye, Therese Umuhoza, Brigitte Umutoni, Fathiah Zakham, Matin Ndayambaje, Benjamin Hewins, Methode Ngabo Gasana, Ali Toloue Ostadgavahi, Gustavo Sganzerla, Fabrice Ndayisenga, David Kelvin, Jean Claude Udahemuka
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundRift Valley Fever (RVF) is a mosquito-borne zoonotic disease that poses a serious threat to both humans and livestock across various regions, particularly in Africa, the Arabian Peninsula, and parts of the Indian Ocean Islands.

title: Latent class analysis for health-related quality of life in nurses in China
creator: Yan Zhao, Bei Yang, Jianying Chu
description: BackgroundThis study aimed to identify the types of quality of life (QoL) based on the five dimensions of the EQ-5D and predict factors affecting QoL.MethodsA multistage stratified cluster sampling survey was conducted among the staff of 12 general hospitals, 1,965 nurses completed the survey, and the data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0 and Mplus 8.3 for latent analysis.

title: MCA-Mamba-2: A Multi-Channel Attention State-Space Network for Ultrasonic Guided Wave Damage Detection in Small-Diameter Pipes
creator: Qiuyu Yu, Ruohua Zhou, Zhengxian Liang, Yajun Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ultrasonic guided wave (UGW) inspection of small-diameter pipes is complicated by the narrow usable frequency band and by strong susceptibility to measurement noise, both of which degrade the reliability of damage identification. This study proposes a multi-channel attention Mamba-2 (MCA-Mamba-2) network that couples a convolutional front end with a bidirectional Mamba-2 state-space backbone and combines multi-head self-attention with channel attention for feature fusion.

title: Virtual friendly visitor program: combatting loneliness in community dwelling older adults
creator: Barbara A. Gordon, Chelsea B. Miceli, Pamela A. Yankeelov, Samantha G. Cotton, Anna C. Faul
description: IntroductionLoneliness is a critical public health issue affecting older adults, with significant impacts on their mental and physical health, including increased risks of depression, cognitive decline, and higher mortality rates, necessitating distinct approaches for each condition given their unique implications and the exacerbation of these issues during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Effects of smoking cessation on individuals with COPD: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Zihan Wang, Yifan Qiu, Xiang Ji, Liang Dong
description: ObjectiveDespite smoking being a significant risk factor in the occurrence and progression of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), no comprehensive analysis has been conducted to determine the potential benefits of smoking cessation for patients with established COPD or identify specific indicators that may be improved.

title: Metabolic reprogramming in ulcerative colitis: integrating dietary drivers, pathogenesis, and therapeutic advances
creator: Yunze Liu, Yisha Wan, Xinyu Lu, Aili Xu, Xia Ding, Yuan Li
description: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a complex disorder characterized by gene–environment interactions that compromise the integrity of the mucosa and submucosa. The current evidence indicates a significant correlation between the increasing incidence of UC and the consumption of a Western diet.

title: Cytokines in narcolepsy type 1: pathogenic relevance, biomarker potential, and future directions
creator: Jingqian Gao, Lijing Jia, Zhenzhen Qu, Xiaoxiao Wang
description: Narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) is a central disorder of hypersomnolence characterized by the selective loss of hypocretin/orexin-producing neurons. Its pathogenesis is closely associated with HLA genetic susceptibility, environmental triggers, and T-cell-mediated autoimmune responses. In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to the role of cytokines in the immunopathology of NT1.

title: The effects of a bioavailable curcumin formulation on Alzheimer's disease pathologies: A potential risk for neuroinflammation
creator: Shaun Cade, Clive Prestidge, Xin‐Fu Zhou, Larisa Bobrovskaya
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a common cause of dementia characterized by the presence of two proteinaceous deposits in the brain. These pathologies may be a consequence of complex interactions between neurons and glia before the onset of cognitive impairments. Curcumin, a bioactive compound found in turmeric, is a promising candidate for AD because it alleviates neuropathologies in mouse models of the disease. Although its clinical efficacy has been hindered by low oral bioavailability, the development of new formulations may overcome this limitation.

title: Beyond the Pain Management Clinic: The Role of AI-Integrated Remote Patient Monitoring in Chronic Disease Management – A Narrative Review
creator: Prachi M Patel, Maja Green, Jennifer Tram, Eugene Wang, Melissa Zhu Murphy, Alaa Abd-Elsayed, Krishnan Chakravarthy
description: Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) stands as a pivotal advancement in patient-centered care, offering substantial improvements in the diagnosis, management, and outcomes of chronic conditions. Through the utilization of advanced digital technologies, RPM facilitates the real-time collection and transmission of critical health data, enabling clinicians to make prompt, informed decisions that enhance patient safety and care, particularly within home environments.

title: Psychological Effects of Noise Exposure on Personnel in Central Sterile Supply Department in China
creator: Wen-Jun Wang, Shu-Ping Zhou, Yun Liang, Chan-Juan Ma, Xin-Cui Wan
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate whether noise exposure in hospital sterile supply centers exacerbated the psychological burden on staff, potentially mediated by concerns about physiological health.MethodsBetween July 5 and August 4, 2023, 308 staffs from central sterile supply departments in 30 hospitals in Hainan were chosen by convenient sampling method.

title: Intermittent and periodic fasting: molecular mechanisms, health benefits and research challenges
creator: Ya Liu, Hongwei Guo
description: Intermittent fasting (IF) and Periodic fasting (PF) are biologically plausible non-pharmacological interventions. They trigger core metabolic reprogramming from glucose catabolism to ketogenesis and activate conserved nutrient-sensing networks including AMPK and sirtuins, coupled with mTOR/IGF-1 axis suppression. Such adaptive regulation enhances cellular repair, antioxidant defense and inflammatory homeostasis, conferring multi-system benefits encompassing metabolic improvement, neuroprotection, anti-tumor activity and healthspan extension.

title: Zuojin Pill Alleviates Precancerous Lesions of Gastric Cancer by Modulating the MEK/ERK/c-Myc Pathway: An Integrated Approach of Network Pharmacology, Molecular Dynamics Simulation, and Experimental Validation
creator: Lan Liang, Chenming He, Xue Han, Jia Liu, Liuhong Yang, Fengjiao Chang, Yami Zhang, Jie Lin
description: BackgroundPrecancerous lesions of gastric cancer (PLGC) represent critical stages in gastric cancer progression, with a high risk of malignancy. Current treatments, such as Helicobacter pylori eradication, show limited efficacy in reversing precancerous molecular changes. Zuojin Pill (ZJP), a traditional Chinese medicine, has demonstrated potential for treating digestive disorders and may offer a promising approach for PLGC intervention.

title: Recent Developments in Drug Design of Oral Synthetic Free Fatty Acid Receptor 1 Agonists
creator: Lei Liu, Qinghua Zhang, Yichuan Ma, Ling Lin, Wenli Liu, Aizhong Ding, Chunjian Wang, Shuiping Zhou, Jinyong Cai, Hai Tang
description: Over the past two decades, synthetic FFAR1 agonists such as TAK-875 and TSL1806 have undergone meticulous design and extensive clinical trials. However, due to issues primarily related to hepatotoxicity, no FFAR1 agonist has yet received regulatory approval. Research into the sources of hepatotoxicity suggests that one potential cause lies in the molecular structure itself.

title: Editorial: The uterus immune microenvironment features in physiological and pathological conditions
creator: Md Zahidul I. Pranjol, Dmitry A. Zinovkin, Anna S. Portyanko, Hongbo Wang
description: myometrium and cervix together constitute one of the most restless immune environments in the human body: a tissue that remodels itself with every cycle, tolerates a semi-allogeneic fetus for nine months, heals without scarring after delivery, and, when this coordination breaks down, gives rise to some of the most common and stubborn disorders in women’s health.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Towards Exercise Therapy Among Patients with Stage 5 Chronic Kidney Disease on Regular Hemodialysis
creator: Ying Chai, Qingping Gu, Lijuan Fan, Ying Lu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundExercise therapy could improve physical and psychological health in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study aimed to investigate knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) towards exercise therapy among patients with CKD stage 5 on regular hemodialysis.MethodsThe cross-sectional study was conducted between August 1st and 30th, 2023; KAP and demographic characteristics of CKD-5 patients were assessed with self-distributed questionnaire and analyzed using logistic regression and structural equation modeling (SEM).

title: Prioritization of Surgical, Obstetric, Trauma, and Anesthesia Care in South and Southeast Asian Countries’ Health Planning and Policy‑making
creator: Saloni Mitra, Ritika Shetty, Shirish Rao, Sweta Dubey, Siddhesh Zadey
description: Background: Lack of policy prioritization of surgical, obstetric, trauma and anesthesia (SOTA) care in South and Southeast Asian countries could be a potential contributor to limited access to care.Objective: To assess the SOTA care prioritization in National Health Policies, Strategies, and Plans (NHPSPs).Methods: We analyzed NHPSPs from twelve South and Southeast Asian countries.

title: Advances in B Cell Targeting for Treating Muscle-Specific Tyrosine Kinase-Associated Myasthenia Gravis
creator: Guanlian Hu, Xue Zhao, Yiren Wang, Xiaoyan Zhu, Zhan Sun, Xiaoxiao Yu, Jiahui Wang, Qian Liu, Jing Zhang, Yingna Zhang, Junhong Yang, Ting Chang, Zhe Ruan, Jie Lv, Feng Gao
description: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a typical autoimmune disease of the nervous system. It is characterized by skeletal muscle weakness and fatigue due to impaired neuromuscular junction transmission mediated by IgG autoantibodies. Muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase-associated MG (MuSK-MG), a rare and severe subtype of MG, is distinguished by the presence of anti-MuSK antibodies; it responds poorly to traditional therapies.

title: Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging in stroke: current applications, limitations, and future directions
creator: Wanxia Wang, Xin Wen, Yuan Zhang, Hongyu Wang, Longhua Hu, Cheng Tan, Zicai Liu
description: Stroke is currently one of the leading causes of death and disability worldwide among neurological diseases. Although traditional imaging techniques can clearly delineate lesion extent and hemorrhagic patterns, they are limited in quantifying microscopic structural changes and repair processes in early-stage brain tissue damage.

title: Therapy-educated fibroblast states link treatment pressure to residual disease and acquired resistance in gastric cancer
creator: Zhigang Chen, Yongtao Yang, Ting Yang, Liping Gao, Ting Zhou, Mengyu Deng
description: Chemotherapy, immune checkpoint blockade, HER2-targeted therapy, and anti-angiogenic therapy have widened treatment options for gastric cancer, yet residual disease and acquired resistance remain common. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are often classified as fixed subtypes, even though treatment exposes them to tissue injury, inflammatory cytokines, hypoxia, altered interstitial pressure, and matrix stress.

title: A Comparative Study Assessing the Incidence and Degree of Hyperkalemia in Patients on Unfractionated Heparin versus Low-Molecular Weight Heparin
creator: Lina Naseralallah, Dima Nasrallah, Somaya Koraysh, Shimaa Aboelbaha, Tarteel Ali Hussain
description: BackgroundHeparin and its derivates, including unfractionated heparin (UFH) and low molecular weight heparin (LMWH), are among the most commonly used anticoagulants. Nonetheless, their use has been associated with hyperkalemia.ObjectiveTo determine and compare the incidence, magnitude, and potential risk factors of hyperkalemia in patients receiving UFH versus LMWH in a real-world clinical setting.

title: Orlistat: a comprehensive review of a lipase inhibitor from obesity management to emerging oncological applications
creator: Li Li, Yuchao Hao
description: Orlistat, a potent inhibitor of gastric and pancreatic lipases, has been a cornerstone of pharmacological obesity management for over 2 decades. By reducing dietary fat absorption, it facilitates modest but clinically significant weight loss and helps prevent weight regain when combined with lifestyle interventions.

title: Adding Dexmedetomidine to Methylene Blue in Thoracic Paravertebral Block for Video-Assisted Lobectomy: A Case Series Study
creator: Francesco Coppolino, Simona Brunetti, Leonardo Maria Bottazzo, Gianluigi Cosenza, Pasquale Sansone, Marco Fiore, Maria Beatrice Passavanti, Vincenzo Pota, Maria Caterina Pace
description: PurposeThoracic surgery often results in severe chronic postoperative pain. Current evidence favors two locoregional techniques. Thoracic Epidural Anesthesia (TEA), the gold standard, and Thoracic Paravertebral Block (TPVB), which is associated with fewer side effects but is limited by short duration of action of local anesthetics (LA) and potential failure due to improper drug distribution.

title: Higher Intraocular Levels of Inflammatory Factors are Related to Retinal Vascular and Neurodegeneration in Myopic Retinopathy
creator: Ling Zeng, Zhikuan Yang, Wei Pan, Ding Lin, Yao Tang, Baihua Chen, Heping Xu, Xiaoning Li
description: PurposeIn this study, we aimed to investigate the relationship between the intraocular levels of inflammatory factors and myopia-related retinal vascular and neuronal degeneration.Patients and MethodsOne hundred and forty-seven patients with Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) implantation were enrolled and all participants received comprehensive ophthalmic examination. About 100~150 ul of aqueous humor was collected immediately before ICL surgery.

title: Indian Shot (Canna Indica L). Leaves Provide Valuable Insights into the Management of Inflammation and Other Associated Disorders Offering Health Benefits
creator: Mohammad Abdullah Taher, Hasin Hasnat, Safaet Alam, Suriya Akter Shompa, Mirola Afroze, Mala Khan, Chuxiao Shao, Shuanghu Wang, Peiwu Geng, Abdullah Al Mamun
description: BackgroundThroughout history, plants have played a crucial role in advancing medicinal treatments by providing a diverse range of compounds for the development of innovative therapies. Canna indica L. a tropical herb of the Cannaceae family, also known as Indian shot, has a rich history of traditional use in treating ailments like inflammation, malaria, dysentery, fever, dropsy, and diarrhea.

title: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy for autoimmune diseases: from exploratory clinical trials to quantitative pharmacodynamic modeling development
creator: Yuqin Sun, Xiao Heng, Guang Hu, Xiumei Bo
description: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy has produced major advances in treating hematologic malignancies. Recently, researchers have explored its use in autoimmune diseases. However, the complex pathogenesis and high heterogeneity of these disorders create substantial uncertainty about treatment efficacy and safety in clinical settings.

title: Correction: The inconsistent effects of tDCS in rehabilitation and cognitive enhancement: sources of variability and paths to personalization
creator: Andrey Timashkov, Sergey Andreev, Anna Safonova, Samira Zangieva, Dzerassa Kadieva, Oksana Zinchenko
description:

This article is an output of a research project HSE-BR-2025-26 implemented an output of the Basic Research Program at HSE University.”

The original version of this article has been updated.

title: Exploring the Role of SMPD3 in the lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA Regulatory Network in TBI Progression by Influencing Energy Metabolism
creator: Changmeng Cui, Biao Xu, Hui Liu, Changshui Wang, Tao Zhang, Pei Jiang, Lei Feng
description: BackgroundTraumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with disturbances in energy metabolism. This study aimed to construct a lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA network through bioinformatics methods to explore energy metabolism-related genes in the pathogenesis of TBI.MethodsData from datasets GSE171718, GSE131695, and GSE223245 obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus, were analyzed to identify differentially expressed (DE) genes.

title: Machine Learning Approach to Classify Vibrio vulnificus Necrotizing Fasciitis, Non-Vibrio Necrotizing Fasciitis and Cellulitis
creator: Chia-Peng Chang, Kai-Hsiang Wu
description: BackgroundRecent advancements in artificial intelligence have led to increased adoption of machine learning in disease identification, particularly for challenging diagnoses like necrotizing fasciitis and Vibrio vulnificus infections. This shift is driven by the technology’s efficiency, objectivity, and accuracy, offering potential solutions to longstanding diagnostic hurdles in clinical practice.MethodsThis investigation incorporated 180 inpatients suffering from soft tissue infections.

title: Toward economically viable green hydrogen production: enhanced catalytic atom-efficiency, dual-functional systems, and non-traditional water sources
creator: Yuru Liu, Pengpeng Wu, Lin Huang, Junyan Yang, Ningning Song, Jiuyang He, Zhanjun Guo, Minmin Liang
description: The light-driven hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) represents a promising renewable energy conversion technology to combat the global energy crisis, particularly as the field shifts toward utilizing abundant water sources including wastewater and seawater rather than freshwater. However, achieving an economically viable levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) requires overcoming several fundamental challenges.

title: Including Health System Capacities into the Assessment Framework of a Temperature-Resilience Health System
creator: Jingyi Zhao, Xiaowei Hao, Xiaofeng Sun, Yajie Du, Meng Zhang, Qing Wang
description: IntroductionThis study includes health system capacities into the assessment framework of a temperature-resilience health system while accounting for system interactions.MethodsIn accordance with the guidelines provided by the World Health Organization, the conceptual framework of a climate-resilient health system has been adopted.

title: Response to “Real-World Healthcare Resource Utilization, Healthcare Costs, and Injurious Falls Among Elderly Patients with Geographic Atrophy” [Letter]
creator: Ahmad Yani Noor, Nurrul Ainy, Harinto Nur Seha
description: nificant clinical and economic burden associated with geographic atrophy (GA) in elderly populations enrolled in Medicare Advantage programs.1 This retrospective study highlights increased healthcare utilization, rising costs, and the rising risk of falls with serious injuries as GA progresses, especially in patients with visual impairment (VI) or blindness (B).

title: Beyond risk management: reconsidering P-OCD in inpatient mental health care
creator: Inga Piotrowska-Chen
description: ense anxiety and shame (2). In its most severe form, OCD can lead to significant self‑neglect, self‑harm, and even suicide attempts (3). OCD may also present as a co‑morbid condition in individuals with psychotic disorders, which can further complicate assessment and treatment (4).

title: Corneal Epithelial Thickness Correlation with Dry Eye Symptom Severity: A Cross-Sectional Study [Response to Letter]
creator: Bruno Barbosa Ribeiro, João Heitor Marques, Pedro Manuel Baptista, Paulo J M Sousa, Saúl Pires, Pedro Menéres, Irene Barbosa
description: s the importance of our research and pushes us forward. However, we would like to address some points: The ANTERION is a high-resolution, anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) with a long wavelength of 1300 nm, allowing precise measurements of the anterior segment.

title: Analysis of smoldering multiple myeloma according to the target of the monoclonal immunoglobulin of patients
creator: Sylvie Hermouet, Nicolas Mennesson, Sophie Allain‐Maillet, Edith Bigot‐Corbel, Andri Olafsson, Brynjar Viðarsson, Páll T. Önundarson, Bjarni A. Agnarsson, Margrét Sigurðardóttir, Ingunn Þorsteinsdóttir, Ísleifur Ólafsson, Elías Eyþórsson, Ásbjörn Jónsson, Thorvardur J. Love, Saemundur Rognvaldsson,
description: 24 Antigenic stimulation initiates subsets of plasma cell dyscrasias, including monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) and multiple myeloma (MM). 1 MGUS and MM are characterized by genetically altered clonal plasma cells that produce large quantities of a single immunoglobulin (Ig), termed “monoclonal Ig (mcIg),” or M‐protein. Smoldering multiple myeloma (SMM) is the intermediate stage between asymptomatic MGUS and MM.

title: Ethics – A matter of principle?
creator: Michael Trimble
description: Discussion of bioethical issues using the four principles approach proposed by Beauchamp and Childress is now standard practice in the UK. This paper first documents the history of principlism before considering its impact and reviewing some criticisms of the approach. A future paper will examine some of the philosophical difficulties arising from principlism in greater depth.

title: Evaluating Performance Among National Basketball Association Players After Jones Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Andrew H Kim, Myung-Jin Cha, Alvina Pan, Gianna Dafflisio, Miguel A Cartagena-Reyes, Frederick Mun, Jonathan R Kaplan, Amiethab A Aiyer
description: Background:In professional basketball, Jones fractures are among the most common cause of lower extremity stress injury. Despite its prevalence, there is a paucity of research on the impact of Jones fractures on athletic performance in the National Basketball Association (NBA).

title: Diagnostic efficacy of aldosterone-to-renin ratio to screen primary aldosteronism in hypertension: a systemic review and meta-analysis
creator: Ting-Wei Kao, Jui-Yi Chen, Jung-Hua Liu, Wen-Hsin Tseng, Chih-Chia Hsieh, Vin-Cent Wu, Yen-Hung Lin, Zheng-Wei Chen
description: Background:The aldosterone-to-renin ratio (ARR) is commonly used for screening primary aldosteronism (PA) in patients with difficult-to-control hypertension. Various thresholds have been proposed for the confirmatory tests, leading to inconsistency in the results.Objectives:This study aimed to elucidate the performance of ARR screening in hypertensive patients.Design:Systemic review and meta-analysis.

title: Healing through faith: spirituality and shrine visitation as coping mechanisms among haemophilia patients in Kashmir—an interpretative phenomenological study
creator: Shabnam Mushtaq, Wakar Amin Zargar, Fayaz Ahmad Paul
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn Kashmir, Sufi traditions are integral to everyday life. Visits to shrines are a culturally significant expression of faith and may influence how individuals cope with lifelong health conditions such as haemophilia.ObjectiveThis study sought to explore the experiences of adults living with haemophilia in Kashmir with spirituality and shrine visitation as coping methods to deal with the psychological, emotional and social challenges of their condition.MethodsA qualitative study using the Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) approach was conducted at the Haemophilia day care centre,

title: Recurrent Heatwaves Slow Down the Recovery of a Phytoplankton Community
creator: Francesco Polazzo, Markus Hermann, Melina Crettaz‐Minaglia, Andreu Rico
description: Heatwaves (HWs) are predicted to increase in frequency and severity due to climate change. Yet, there is limited information about how ecological resilience of aquatic communities is going to be impacted by recurrent HWs. Here, we used data from an outdoor freshwater mesocosm experiment where a semi‐natural phytoplankton community was exposed to three subsequent HWs.

title: Causal associations of immunophenotypes with metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease and mediating pathways: a Mendelian randomization study
creator: Kexin Xie, Ming Chen, Hongjin An, Jinhang Gao, Chengwei Tang, Zhiyin Huang
description: Background:Increasing evidence suggests that immunophenotypes play a crucial role in Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD), but the specific immunophenotypes contributing to its pathogenesis remain unclear.Objectives:This study aimed to elucidate the causal associations between immunophenotypes and MAFLD and identify the underlying mediation pathways involved.Design:Mendelian randomization (MR) study.

title: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder among civilians in Indian-administered Kashmir: a systematic review
creator: Tamkeen Sakeena, Aneeza Pervez, Cecilie Lolansen
description: PurposeProlonged exposure to armed conflict is associated with elevated rates of PTSD in civilian populations, such as Indian-administered Kashmir. This review aimed to systematically synthesise research on prevalence, risk factors, and correlates of PTSD among civilians in this setting and their association with armed conflict exposure.MethodsA systematic review following PRISMA guidelines was conducted for empirical studies published up to 2025.

title: Predictive role of neuron-specific enolase and S100-β in early neurological deterioration and unfavorable prognosis in patients with ischemic stroke
creator: Ruishu Jiang, Youlian Lai
description: BackgroundWe aimed to assess whether neuron-specific enolase (NSE) and S100-β levels are associated with early neurological deterioration (END) in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).MethodsWe conducted a prospective study between March 2022 and October 2023 in 286 patients with AIS.

title: Peripheral exosomal miRNAs as candidate molecular indicators associated with acupuncture at ST36 in an LPS-induced neuroinflammation model
creator: Seung-Nam Kim
description: This study aimed to identify circulating exosomal microRNA (miRNA) candidates showing a control-like expression pattern following ST36 acupuncture treatment in an LPS-induced neuroinflammation model, using empirical Bayes reanalysis of previously published microarray data. Two independent Affymetrix GeneChip miRNA 4.0 microarray datasets from C57BL/6 male mice were reanalysed using the limma empirical Bayes framework with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction.

title: Patient flow analysis with fast-track MRI for suspected stroke in the emergency department and associated non-comprehensive stroke center
creator: Malini Vendela Sagar, Karen Lind Gandrup, Diane Jensen, Christian Hedeager Krag, Mikael Ploug Boesen, Henriette Raaschou, Helle Collatz Christensen, Christina Kruuse
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background:Good outcomes in stroke care require swift diagnostics, for which magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as first-line brain imaging is superior to computed tomography scans. Reduced length of stay (LOS) in hospital and emergency departments (ED) may optimize resource use.

title: Privacy-aware learning analytics for exploratory behavior through federated and explainable AI
creator: Rommel Gutierrez, Aracely Mera-Navarrete, Ana Cristina Villegas, Vanessa Guevara, William Villegas-Ch
description: Learning analytics platforms increasingly use behavioral traces to model engagement, navigation, and self-directed learning dynamics in virtual learning environments (VLEs). However, most current approaches prioritize predictive accuracy, centralize sensitive student records, and rarely analyze the stability of exploratory representations under distributed configurations.

title: Protocol for establishing CRISPR-Cas12a for efficient genome editing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa phages
creator: Bingjie Yan, Yujia Liu, Yumei Cai, Yuqing Liu, Yibao Chen
description: SummaryWe developed an efficient type V CRISPR-Cas12a system tailored specifically for Pseudomonas aeruginosa phages, showcasing its remarkable cleavage activity and the ability to precisely introduce genetic modifications, including point mutations, deletions, and insertions, into phage genomes. Here, we present a protocol for establishing CRISPR-Cas12a for genome editing of Pseudomonas aeruginosa phages.

title: Development and internal validation of a macrophage migration inhibitory factor-based risk assessment model for delayed cerebral ischemia in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
creator: JianBo Zhang, ChengMing Bao, AnKui Lu, Kun Guo
description: BackgroundDelayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) is an important cause of poor outcomes in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) is involved in the regulation of inflammatory responses and may be associated with the development of DCI after aSAH.

title: Learning on the job? Foraging strategies of juvenile versus adult Lesser black-backed gulls at their first migratory stopover
creator: Mélibée Morel, Reinoud Allaert, Eric Stienen, Ruben Fijn, Frederick Verbruggen, Wendt Müller, Luc Lens
description: Developing efficient foraging strategies is critical for survival, especially during the high-mortality post-fledging period in birds. This period is particularly challenging for migratory species, where juveniles must navigate unfamiliar environments with limited experience and knowledge. Our study focused on the foraging strategies of 20 juvenile lesser black-backed gulls (Larus fuscus) during the first 20 days of their initial migratory stopover.

title: Perspectives of La0.9Sr0.1Fe0.9Co0.1O3±δ perovskite obtained by Pechini and sonochemical methods: a case study
creator: Gloria E. de la Huerta-Hernández, Tatiana Rodríguez-Flores, Armando Reyes-Montero, Iván Castro-Cisneros, Isaías Hernández-Pérez, José A. Chávez-Carvayar
description: The sonochemical method is a novel synthesis route that takes advantage of the use of ultrasonic radiation to obtain different nanomaterials with an improvement in the process variables and material characteristics. In this work, two different synthesis routes to obtain a double perovskite structure were compared in detail.

title: Genome-guided prebiotic fermentation generates anti-virulence metabolites against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
creator: Rasha Elsayim, Monerah S. M. Alqahtani, Malak Muhayya Alosaimi, Alaa Alnoor Alameen, Dalia Al Sarar, Ejlal Mohamed Abdullah, Esra’a Abudouleh
description: BackgroundThe rise of multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa has heightened interest in microbiome-based anti-virulence strategies that mitigate pathogenicity without directly affecting bacterial survival. This study examined whether the fermentation of Arabic gum and baobab by probiotic bacteria produces metabolites that reduce P. aeruginosa virulence.MethodsThe carbohydrate-active enzyme profiles of Bifidobacterium longum, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum, and P.

title: Social interactions do not affect mycoplasma infection in griffon vultures
creator: Elvira D'Bastiani, Nili Anglister, Inna Lysnyansky, Inna Mikula, Marta Acácio, Gideon Vaadia, Kaija Gahm, Orr Spiegel, Noa Pinter-Wollman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Uncovering the ways in which pathogens spread has important implications for population health and management. Pathogen transmission is influenced by various factors, including patterns of social interactions and shared use of space. We aim to understand how the social behaviour of griffon vultures (Gyps fulvus), a species of conservation interest, influences the presence or absence of mycoplasma, a group of bacteria known to cause respiratory diseases in birds.

title: Uncommon presentation of Haemophilus parainfluenzae bacteremia: A case study on aortic valve endocarditis
creator: Nasrin Dhapa, Hannah Rodriguez, Zachary Visinoni, Neeladri Misra, Diwakar Lingam
description: Haemophilus parainfluenzae, a HACEK organism, is one of five species known to less commonly cause infective endocarditis. This article presents a rare and noteworthy case of H. parainfluenzae endocarditis affecting the aortic valve, seemingly unique when Haemophilus species in endocarditis were previously known to more commonly involve the pulmonic or mitral valves. In the setting of H.

title: Functional characterization of AtAAS as a 5-hydroxytryptophan decarboxylase linking serotonin formation to melatonin metabolism in Arabidopsis thaliana
creator: Xiaohao Guo, Siyu Lin, Chuan Dong, Xinyu Huang, Hailian Hu, Baohai Li, Yuanyuan Tan, Qingyao Shu
description: IntroductionSerotonin and melatonin are plant signaling molecules involved in growth, stress responses, and redox balance. While animals produce serotonin via 5‑hydroxytryptophan (5‑HTP), plants are thought to use the tryptamine pathway. Although 5‑HTP exists in plants, its conversion to serotonin lacks a genetically defined enzyme.

title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis mimicking multisystem pyoderma gangrenosum: A case report
creator: Amanda Gormley, Peter Green
description: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis, a type of small-medium vessel vasculitis, can pose diagnostic challenges due to its diverse clinical manifestations. We present a case that mimicked multisystem pyoderma gangrenosum with cutaneous ulceration, renal sparing, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody negativity. Although antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody is positive in approximately 90% of cases of granulomatosis with polyangiitis, its negativity should not exclude the diagnosis.

title: GIN-TONIC: non-hierarchical full-text indexing for graph genomes
creator: Ünsal Öztürk, Marco Mattavelli, Paolo Ribeca
description: This paper presents a new data structure, GIN-TONIC (Graph INdexing Through Optimal Near Interval Compaction), designed to index arbitrary string-labelled directed graphs representing, for instance, pangenomes or transcriptomes. GIN-TONIC provides several capabilities not offered by other graph-indexing methods based on the FM-Index.

title: Revised safety evaluation of the food enzyme glucose oxidase from the genetically modified Trichoderma reesei strain AR‐352
creator: EFSA Panel on Food Enzymes (FEZ), Holger Zorn, José Manuel Barat Baviera, Claudia Bolognesi, Francesco Catania, Gabriele Gadermaier, Ralf Greiner, Baltasar Mayo, Alicja Mortensen, Yrjö Henrik Roos, Marize L M Solano, Monika Sramkova, Henk Van Loveren, Laurence Vernis, Jaime Aguilera, Yi Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The food enzyme glucose oxidase (β‐d‐glucose: oxygen 1‐oxidoreductase; EC 1.1.3.4) is produced with the genetically modified Trichoderma reesei strain AR‐352 by AB Enzymes GmbH. In a previous opinion, the Panel on Food Contact Materials, Enzymes and Processing Aids of the European Food Safety Authority could not conclude on the absence of recombinant DNA from the production strain in the food enzyme due to uncertainties about the limit of detection of the applied methodology.

title: A dynamic customized electronic health record rule based clinical decision support tool for standardized adult intensive care metrics
creator: Eric W Cucchi, Joseph Burzynski, Nicholas Marshall, Bruce Greenberg
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesMany routine patient care items should be reviewed at least daily for intensive care unit (ICU) patients. These items are often incompletely performed, and dynamic clinical decision support tools (CDSTs) may improve attention to these daily items.

title: Perceived societal meritocratic climate and self-stigma among adolescents in conflict with the law: the mediating role of collective self-esteem and social disconnection
creator: Xiaoyi Wang, Wanlu Li, Rong Liu, Xue Zhang, Weijie Meng
description: IntroductionThis research investigated the relationship between perceived meritocratic climate and self-stigma among adolescents in conflict with the law across two studies.MethodsStudy 1 (N = 322) employed a cross-sectional survey; Study 2 (N = 254) used an experimental manipulation of perceived (non)meritocratic climate.

title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of puerarin on intervertebral disc degeneration by regulating apoptosis of nucleus pulposus cells
creator: Xiaoqiang Wang, Chao Song, Daqian Zhou, Yongliang Mei, Weiye Cai, Rui Chen, Jiale Lv, Houyin Shi, Zongchao Liu
description: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) stands as a prevalent chronic orthopedic ailment, profoundly impacting patients' well‐being due to incapacitating low back pain. Studies have highlighted a close correlation between IVDD and the programmed cell death of nucleus pulposus (NP) cells orchestrated by interleukin‐1 beta (IL‐1β), tumor necrosis factor‐alpha (TNF‐α), and caspase‐3 (CASP3).

title: Case Report: Reconciling genomic ambiguity with clinical certainty in refractory panniculitis
creator: Sayan Mukherjee, Rajat K. Sahu, Nidhish M. Chandra, Urmila Dhakad, Puneet Kumar
description: Panniculitis in adolescents often poses a diagnostic challenge for physicians. We report an adolescent girl presenting with recurrent steroid-responsive lymphocytic septal panniculitis, genital ulcer, and constitutional symptoms, later complicated by macrophage activation syndrome and steatohepatitis. Extensive evaluation excluded infectious, autoimmune, and malignant causes. Histopathology revealed septal panniculitis without vasculitis or atypical lymphoid cells.

title: Ameboma, a rare cause of intestinal obstruction in bariatric surgery patients: a case report
creator: Mauricio Palacios, Alex Guachilema R, Andrea Lisintuña, Julio Yepez, Sergio Verboonen
description: Ameboma is a rare complication of invasive amebiases caused by the intestinal protozoan Entamoeba histolytica. The disease is characterized by tumorous, exophytic, inflammatory masses in the lower-right quadrant of the abdomen. Symptoms are nonspecific but may include intestinal obstruction and gastrointestinal bleeding. Although computed tomography and ultrasound can identify colonic masses, biopsy is the most accurate diagnostic method for ameboma.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of pembrolizumab plus trastuzumab and chemotherapy as first-line treatment for HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
creator: Haoyu Yang, Weihao Ge, Shuxian Jiang, Xin Lan, Xinting Du
description: ObjectivesThe final analysis of KEYNOTE-811 demonstrated that pembrolizumab plus trastuzumab and chemotherapy significantly improved both overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) compared to trastuzumab plus chemotherapy alone. Based on these latest findings, this study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of pembrolizumab plus trastuzumab and chemotherapy from the perspective of the Chinese healthcare system.

title: Chemistry and properties of fluorescent pyrazole derivatives: an approach to bioimaging applications†
creator: Santiago Melo-Hernández, María-Camila Ríos, Jaime Portilla
description: Fluorescent bioimaging is a crucial technique for in vivo studies in real cell samples, providing vital information about the metabolism of ions or molecules of biological and pharmaceutical significance. This technique typically uses probes based on organic small-molecule fluorophores, with N-heteroaromatic scaffolds playing an essential role due to their exceptional electronic properties and biocompatibility.

title: Analysis of ocular biometrics in cataract patients aged 40 and above in Suzhou, China
creator: Yanfeng Zeng, Wei Song, Quan Yuan, Xiaoqin Wang, Yana Ma, Huan Hu
description: PurposeThis cross-sectional study investigated the distribution of ocular biometric parameters in cataract patients aged ≥40 years from East China, with a specific focus on age- and sex-related differences and their correlations. Given the paucity of large-sample reference data for this population, we aimed to establish a localized framework to support precise surgical planning in refractive cataract surgery.

title: A case of peripartum cardiomyopathy in dichorionic diamniotic twin pregnancy
creator: Kanis Fatema, Zhi Ying Tan, Uduwarage Ranaweera
description: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is an uncommon life-threatening condition that is characterized by heart failure with reduced ejection fraction during late pregnancy or within 5 months of postpartum in the absence of other causes of heart failure. Despite advances in managing PPCM, the pathophysiology of it is still poorly understood.

title: Editorial: Integrative OMICS approaches in cancer biology: from molecular mechanisms to precision medicine
creator: Rajiv Pathak, Vibhav Gautam, Rajiv Kumar, Lalit Kumar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). rapid evolution of high-throughput OMICS technologies, including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, epigenomics, metabolomics, and single-cell profiling, has significantly advanced cancer research by enabling comprehensive characterization of tumors across multiple molecular layers and biological scales (3–5). Integrating these complementary OMICS datasets has improved our understanding of the molecular basis of tumor heterogeneity, enabling the identification of clinically relevant biomarkers, improved tumor classification, and new therapeutic targets to support precision oncology (6–9).

title: Association of serum magnesium levels with the risk of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and sepsis in hospitalized patients with cirrhosis: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Xiang-Jie Duan, Yang Cai, Qing Su, Qin Zhou, Man Li, Jin-Lian Chen, Chang-Yun Zhang, Duo-Meng Yang, Hai-Yan Yin, Wan-Jie Gu
description: BackgroundHypomagnesemia is common in patients with cirrhosis. This study aimed to examine the association between serum magnesium levels and the risks of hospital-acquired spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (HA-SBP) and sepsis.MethodsThis retrospective study included patients with cirrhosis who were hospitalized at the First People’s Hospital of Changde City, China, between May 2021 and June 2025.

title: Editorial: Linking knowledge across borders: science diasporas and global south development
creator: Luisa F. Echeverría-King, Kleinsy Bonilla, Branislav Pantović, Efraín Bámaca-López, Ana Maria Carneiro, Derya Buyuktanir Karacan
description: capabilities are often among the most affected by the international outflow of highly skilled talent (Docquier et al., 2007). Namely, many scientific systems in the Global South operate with inadequate or unstable funding, uneven access to research infrastructure, limited career opportunities, and restricted influence over the networks and funding structures that shape international research agendas and opportunities (OECD, 2023, p.

title: Surveillance of CTX-M group 1-producing Enterobacterales at the migratory Little Stint (Calidris minuta)–goat–aquatic interface in the Kenyan Rift Valley: a One Health approach
creator: Catherine W. Mbuthia, Rael J. Too, Alexanda Mzula, Anita Chepkemei, John Kiiru, Samuel Kariuki, Abubakar S. Hoza
description: The escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among critical-priority, extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing pathogens poses a global public health threat. Applying a One Health framework, this study characterized CTX-M Group 1 gene variants alongside co-carried β-lactamase gene families (blaOXA1 − like, blaSHV, and blaTEM) in Enterobacterales across the migratory shorebirds Little Stints (Calidris minuta)-livestock-aquatic interface in the Kenyan Rift Valley.

title: Neurological involvement in localized scleroderma: a systematic review of clinical manifestations and neuroimaging findings
creator: Yuming Chong, Wangfei Mo, Congcong Deng, Nanze Yu, Zenan Xia, Xiao Long
description: BackgroundLocalized scleroderma (LoS) is an autoimmune disorder leading to skin sclerosis and subcutaneous tissue atrophy. Apart from the disfiguring craniofacial lesions, the extracutaneous involvement in LoS has been increasingly recognized and studied. Among all, neurological involvement is common and worth special attention.ObjectivesThis systematic review summarizes the neurological symptoms, neuroimaging findings, and other complementary examination results of LoS.

title: Intravitreal ranibizumab as an adjunct to conventional surgery for neovascular glaucoma: a retrospective observational study of efficacy and clinical characteristics of surgical failure cases
creator: Dan Li, Chao Li, Qing Ye
description: BackgroundIntractable neovascular glaucoma (NVG), secondary to retinal ischemia, responds poorly to traditional surgery due to postoperative neovascularization and scarring. Intravitreal ranibizumab(IVR) swiftly alleviates neovascularization to enable subsequent treatment, yet its long-term efficacy remains unclear.AimThis study sought to evaluate the ranibizumab-surgery combination therapy in NVG and describe clinical characteristics of surgical failure cases.

title: Policy brief: how can rehabilitation be strengthened in Switzerland? Evidence-informed policy considerations based on the 2023 World Health Assembly resolution on strengthening rehabilitation in health systems
creator: Roxanne Maritz, David Weisstanner, Gerold Stucki, Oliver Stoller, Anke Scheel-Sailer, Christian Sturzenegger, Carla Sabariego, The Center for Rehabilitation in Global Health Systems, The Advisory Board of the LIFE Forum Rehabilitation
description: BackgroundRehabilitation needs in Switzerland are rising due to population ageing and the growing prevalence of non-communicable diseases. Yet, these needs are not comprehensively met and rehabilitation remains underrepresented in national strategies. Given the 2023 WHA Resolution on Rehabilitation, there is a growing need to understand how rehabilitation can be strengthened in Switzerland.

title: Comparative efficacy of AAC and ibuprofen versus lasmiditan, ubrogepant, and rimegepant for the acute treatment of episodic migraine in adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
creator: Ashoke Mitra, Billy Franks, Richard Petruschke, Abhijeet Dhiman, Nitu Bansal
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundA range of pharmacologic options is available for acute migraine treatment, yet the efficacy and safety of commonly used over-the-counter (OTC) therapies relative to newer prescription agents remain unclear. Given the scarcity of direct head-to-head trials, this network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluated selected OTC therapies against newer oral agents, including CGRP antagonists and the 5-HT1F receptor agonist.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL for RCTs of acute migraine therapies published between January 1990 and

title: Prognostic value of soluble ST2 in cardiac magnetic resonance defined myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
creator: Chenchen Cui, Donglin Liu, Mingchang Du, Peng Lu, Yu Yang, Lei Chen, Wensu Chen, Min Zhang
description: BackgroundCardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays an essential role in identifying the underlying etiology of myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA). However, risk stratification in patients with CMR-confirmed MINOCA remains insufficiently defined. Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2), a biomarker related to myocardial fibrosis and adverse cardiac remodeling, may provide additional prognostic information in this population.

title: Clinical features of Q fever vertebral osteomyelitis: case reports and literature review
creator: Tao Zhang, Hong Liang Gao, Hua Liu, Song Kai Li
description: BackgroundThis study aims to characterize Q fever vertebral osteomyelitis based on our experience and literature review.MethodsBy reviewing all reported cases of Q fever vertebral osteomyelitis since the 21st century, we characterized the exposure history, clinical presentations, treatment strategies, and prognostic outcomes.ResultsFifty cases of Q fever vertebral osteomyelitis were identified. The mean age was 63.4 ± 15.

title: Effects of rapid weight loss and rapid weight regain on oxidant status and muscle damage in judo athletes
creator: Büşra Özdek, Hamza Budak, Emre Karaduman, Eda Karaduman, Mahmut Esat Uzun, Ali Kerim Yılmaz
description: BackgroundAthletes in weight-class sports frequently use rapid weight loss (RWL) before the official weigh-in to compete in a lower weight category and potentially gain a competitive advantage. After the weigh-in, rapid weight regain (RWG) is commonly applied to restore body mass before competition. However, repeated weight cycling may impair physiological functions, including redox homeostasis and muscle integrity.

title: Dietary phytochemical index and biomarker profiles are associated with colorectal cancer odds: integrating dietary intake with blood biomarkers
creator: Juan Wu, Yubao Song, Meiyan Gao, Junwu Duan, Xuanxuan Ma, Dan Xue, Chengyan Zhang
description: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge. Phytochemical-rich diets may influence colorectal carcinogenesis through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, metabolic, and gut barrier-related mechanisms. However, evidence simultaneously integrating dietary phytochemical intake with other biologically relevant markers remains limited. This study investigated the association between the dietary Phytochemical Index (PI) and CRC odds.

title: Initiators for Continuous Activator Regeneration (ICAR) Depolymerization
creator: Glen R. Jones, Maria-Nefeli Antonopoulou, Nghia P. Truong, Athina Anastasaki
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Chemical recycling of polymers synthesized by atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) typically requires high temperatures (i.e., 170 °C) to operate effectively, not only consuming unnecessary energy but also compromising depolymerization yields due to unavoidable end-group deterioration. To overcome this, the concept of initiators for continuous activator regeneration (ICAR) depolymerization is introduced herein as a broadly applicable approach to significantly reduce reaction temperatures for ATRP depolymerizations.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning model based on multi-source clinical data for predicting the risk of early neurological deterioration in patients with ischemic stroke
creator: Yue Li, Wei Wang, Yilan Wei, Jing Han, Yuan Shi, Quping Ouyang
description: Background and objectiveEarly neurological deterioration (END) is a critical clinical event associated with poor patient outcomes after acute ischemic stroke. Early identification of high-risk patients is crucial for timely clinical management. This study aimed to develop and validate a model for predicting END risk for acute ischemic stroke patients using machine learning algorithms.

title: DNA methylation-based analysis reveals accelerated epigenetic aging in giant cell-enriched adult-type glioblastoma
creator: Pinar Cakmak, Philipp Jurmeister, Iris Divé, Pia S. Zeiner, Joachim P. Steinbach, Tim R. Fenton, Karl H. Plate, Marcus Czabanka, Patrick N. Harter, Katharina J. Weber
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundGiant cell (gc)-enriched glioblastoma (gcGB) represents a distinct histological variant of isocitrate dehydrogenase wild-type adult-type glioblastoma with notable enlarged mono- or multinuclear tumor cells. While some studies suggest a survival advantage for gcGB patients, the underlying causes remain elusive. GcGBs are associated with TP53 mutations, and gcs were shown to accumulate DNA double-strand breaks and show deficient mitosis, potentially triggering cellular senescence programs.

title: Implementation and user acceptance of a domestic robot-assisted surgical training system: a pilot educational study at the first clinical medical college of Jinan university
creator: Wenming Shao, Jianfan Chen, Yidan Wang, Weijie Liu, Jixin Yang, Hui Zhao, Mingya Zhang
description: ObjectiveRobot-assisted surgical systems are being increasingly utilized in the field of surgery, and have been reported to offer enhanced 3D visualization, force feedback, superior ergonomics for the surgeon, and improved operative precision, which collectively may contribute to minimally invasive outcomes and expedited postoperative recovery. However, the integration of robot-assisted technology into surgical training curricula in Chinese medical colleges remains limited.

title: A stable zeolite with atomically ordered and interconnected mesopore channel
creator: Peng Lu, Jiaoyan Xu, Yiqing Sun, Rémy Guillet-Nicolas, Tom Willhammar, Mohammad Fahda, Eddy Dib, Bo Wang, Zhengxing Qin, Hongyi Xu, Jung Cho, Zhaopeng Liu, Haijun Yu, Xiaobo Yang, Qiaolin Lang, Svetlana Mintova, Xiaodong Zou, Valentin Valtchev
description: Zeolites are crystalline microporous materials constructed by corner-sharing tetrahedra (SiO4 and AlO4), with many industrial applications as ion exchangers, adsorbents and heterogeneous catalysts1–4. However, the presence of micropores impedes the use of zeolites in areas dealing with bulky substrates. Introducing extrinsic mesopores, that is, intercrystal/intracrystal mesopores, in zeolites is a solution to overcome the diffusion barrier5–8.

title: Tenecteplase in acute ischemic stroke: an updated meta-analysis
creator: Hussain Almohammed, Ahmed Salah Morad, Bushra Wadi Bin Saddiq, Fatimah Ibrahim Almuhaysin, Bayan Mohammed Khair Al Zoabi, Wejdan Ahmed Aldawsari, Tanveer Nidal Khan, Husna Irfan Thalib, Zainab Alabdi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionTenecteplase (TNK) has emerged as a promising alternative to alteplase (tPA) for intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke (AIS).
